step1_analysis.description: A resonant tank circuit for a 6.78 MHz wireless power receiver. It consists of an inductor and capacitor tuned to the operating frequency to maximize power transfer efficiency.

paper_reference.title: A Resonant Regulating Rectifier (3R) Operating at 6.78 MHz for a 6W Wireless Charger with 86% Efficiency

resonant_frequency.description: The frequency at which the LC tank resonates, maximizing its impedance.

sky130_expected.calculation: f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). With L=1uH and C=551pF, f ≈ 6.78 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The tank must be tuned to the ISM band frequency of 6.78 MHz for standard wireless charging applications.

peak_impedance.description: The maximum impedance of the tank at resonance, determined by the parasitic resistance (Q factor).

sky130_expected.calculation: Z_peak = R_loss. Assuming a parallel loss resistance of 1k ohm.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the quality factor (Q) of the integrated or external inductor used in the design.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the resonant frequency and peak impedance of the LC tank.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Resonant Tank Testbench

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param L_val=1u
.param C_val=551p

* DUT (Values appended to generic netlist for simulation)
LRS N0 GND {L_val}
C1 VXH GND 1n
CRS N0 GND {C_val}
* CLM GND GND (Shorted component commented out)
* SW (GND GND) switch_ideal (Invalid/shorted switch commented out)

* Excitation and Parasitics
Iac GND N0 AC 1
Rloss N0 GND 1k

.control
ac dec 100 1Meg 20Meg

* Calculate impedance magnitude
let z_mag = abs(v(N0))

* Measure peak impedance and resonant frequency
meas ac z_max MAX z_mag
meas ac f_res MAX_AT z_mag

print f_res
print z_max

quit
.endc
.end
